sent_emails.subject: Wannawong Carbon Project at Risk
sent_emails.body: Hi Tom, I just wanted to check in to see how you found the project proposal? Are looking to move forward with it? The reason for my continued follow ups is there are time sensitivities around eligible activities. If you implement the project activities this cropping season and have not registered and had the project declared, there will be additional complexities in showing the required on farm changes that must commence after the project has been declared. This could lead to more questions about the 'newness' component of eligible activities and increases the risk of credits not being awarded and workload required from you to show change to have ACCUs issued. AgriProve are experts in helping our farmers meet these requirements smoothly and without fuss, however we strongly suggest moving your project forward as quickly as possible to avoid additional complexities. I couldn’t miss the opportunity to let you know about this: Queensland producers Kylie and Lance Stephenson have been credited an average of 3.9ACCUs/Ha/Yr using their Droughtmaster herd as the tool! At current ACCU prices that's $136 dollars more per hectare per year. Now, they are using direct to satellite Ceres Tags for precision grazing management. Ceres Devices can be purchased on the AgriProve Market Place and visualised on the AgriProve Platform’s ‘Ready Graze’ tool at no upfront cost by using your projects future ACCUs (credits) for deferred payment financing - find out more here: https://app.agriprove.io/marketplace I'd be keen to learn more about your situation, do you have 5 minutes to connect? I couldn’t miss the opportunity to let you know about this: Queensland producers Kylie and Lance Stephenson have been credited an average of 3.9ACCUs/Ha/Yr using their Droughtmaster herd as the tool! At current ACCU prices that's $136 dollars more per hectare per year. Now, they are using direct to satellite Ceres Tags for precision grazing management. Ceres Devices can be purchased on the AgriProve Market Place and visualised on the AgriProve Platform’s ‘Ready Graze’ tool at no upfront cost by using your projects future ACCUs (credits) for deferred payment financing - find out more here: https://app.agriprove.io/marketplace I'd be keen to learn more about your situation, do you have 5 minutes to connect? I couldn’t miss the opportunity to let you know about this: Queensland producers Kylie and Lance Stephenson have been credited an average of 3.9ACCUs/Ha/Yr using their Droughtmaster herd as the tool! At current ACCU prices that's $136 dollars more per hectare per year. Now, they are using direct to satellite Ceres Tags for precision grazing management. Ceres Devices can be purchased on the AgriProve Market Place and visualised on the AgriProve Platform’s ‘Ready Graze’ tool at no upfront cost by using your projects future ACCUs (credits) for deferred payment financing - find out more here: https://app.agriprove.io/marketplace I'd be keen to learn more about your situation, do you have 5 minutes to connect? I hope to hear from you! I couldn’t miss the opportunity to let you know about this: Queensland producers Kylie and Lance Stephenson have been credited an average of 3.9ACCUs/Ha/Yr using their Droughtmaster herd as the tool! At current ACCU prices that's $136 dollars more per hectare per year. Now, they are using direct to satellite Ceres Tags for precision grazing management. Ceres Devices can be purchased on the AgriProve Market Place and visualised on the AgriProve Platform’s ‘Ready Graze’ tool at no upfront cost by using your projects future ACCUs (credits) for deferred payment financing - find out more here: https://app.agriprove.io/marketplace I'd be keen to learn more about your situation, do you have 5 minutes to connect? I couldn’t miss the opportunity to let you know about this: Queensland producers Kylie and Lance Stephenson have been credited an average of 3.9ACCUs/Ha/Yr using their Droughtmaster herd as the tool! At current ACCU prices that's $136 dollars more per hectare per year. Now, they are using direct to satellite Ceres Tags for precision grazing management. Ceres Devices can be purchased on the AgriProve Market Place and visualised on the AgriProve Platform’s ‘Ready Graze’ tool at no upfront cost by using your projects future ACCUs (credits) for deferred payment financing - find out more here: https://app.agriprove.io/marketplace I'd be keen to learn more about your situation, do you have 5 minutes to connect? I hope to hear from you! I couldn’t miss the opportunity to let you know about this: Queensland producers Kylie and Lance Stephenson have been credited an average of 3.9ACCUs/Ha/Yr using their Droughtmaster herd as the tool! At current ACCU prices that's $136 dollars more per hectare per year. Now, they are using direct to satellite Ceres Tags for precision grazing management. Ceres Devices can be purchased on the AgriProve Market Place and visualised on the AgriProve Platform’s ‘Ready Graze’ tool at no upfront cost by using your projects future ACCUs (credits) for deferred payment financing - find out more here: https://app.agriprove.io/marketplace I'd be keen to learn more about your situation, do you have 5 minutes to connect? I hope to hear from you! I couldn’t miss the opportunity to let you know about this: Queensland producers Kylie and Lance Stephenson have been credited an average of 3.9ACCUs/Ha/Yr using their Droughtmaster herd as the tool! At current ACCU prices that's $136 dollars more per hectare per year. Now, they are using direct to satellite Ceres Tags for precision grazing management. Ceres Devices can be purchased on the AgriProve Market Place and visualised on the AgriProve Platform’s ‘Ready Graze’ tool at no upfront cost by using your projects future ACCUs (credits) for deferred payment financing - find out more here: https://app.agriprove.io/marketplace I'd be keen to learn more about your situation, do you have 5 minutes to connect? I couldn’t miss the opportunity to let you know about this: Queensland producers Kylie and Lance Stephenson have been credited an average of 3.9ACCUs/Ha/Yr using their Droughtmaster herd as the tool! At current ACCU prices that's $136 dollars more per hectare per year. Now, they are using direct to satellite Ceres Tags for precision grazing management. Ceres Devices can be purchased on the AgriProve Market Place and visualised on the AgriProve Platform’s ‘Ready Graze’ tool at no upfront cost by using your projects future ACCUs (credits) for deferred payment financing - find out more here: https://app.agriprove.io/marketplace. I wanted to personally reach out, as I found your email on the Simmentals website and thought you might be interested to hear that a graziers like yourself, used their stud and commercial herd to generate a whopping $233,000 in soil carbon credits on 500ha in under 2 years. sent_emails.subject: Re: Contract
sent_emails.body: Hi Geoff and Lyndal, Thank you for your email. Please see my responses below to the questions raised yesterday on the phone and in your follow up email, with direct reference to the Key Commercial Terms and Master Terms (attached). AgriProve success fee. As detailed in the "AgriProve Remuneration" section on page 5 of the Key Commercial Terms, AgriProve Fee for this contract is 25% of all Project ACCUs and Project Co-benefits (for more on co-benefits refer to 9.2 of the Master Terms). Market Adjustment of AgriProve Fee states "Where this Market Offer Price is less than the AgriProve Fee under this Agreement, the AgriProve Fee will be reduced to the Market Offer". This means should the AgriProve Fee decrease, you will get the benefit of this under your contract. You are signing this contract with the understanding of a 25% AgriProve Fee, which cannot be arbitrarily increased, with the contract strictly omitting any ability to do so This is further controlled for by Clause 21 of the Master Terms and Conditions stating "AgriProve may amend the Master T&Cs from time to time... provided any amendments have no material adverse effect on Landholder or Operator". Sale of ACCUs through AgriProve as broker. AgriProve can help broker the sale of ACCUs for you, however, you are able to broker your own transaction without AgriProve acting as broker. No where in the contract are you bound to using AgriProve in brokering your ACCU transactions. If you choose to hold your own ACCUs, clause 8.2 of the Master T's & C's states AgriProve must transfer Project ACCUs to the Registry Account (Australian National Registry of Emissions Units (ANREU)) of the parties who are entitled to those project ACCUs. Please note that while it is not part of our obligations under the contract, AgriProve can assist you in setting up your own ANREU account. Partnering producers typically select Standard Option 2 or 3 on page 6 of the Key Commercial Terms as they are re-negotiable at anytime. Once your ANREU account is set up (typically this is done once we have measured an increase), we can switch to the distribution of your ACCUs to your ANREU account. For clarity, there are two mentions of brokerage in the Master T's and C's. The first is clause 11.4 which states in the event that Option 2 or Option 3 is pursued there is a brokerage fee. The second is clause 12.3 stating that the funds of the sales we broker must be transferred to you in 2 Business days (less brokerage). Default and Termination Yes, termination by the Operator will mean transferring to AgriProve the number of ACCU's issued to date. This is explained in clause 14.3.3 of the Master T's & C's. AgriProve will then give these all back to the regulator (we don't keep them) and terminate the project. To further explain; the soil carbon methodology requires projects to be monitored for 25 years. If you (the operator) choose to terminate the project prior to 25 years, the methodology requires all issued ACCUs to be returned, and this is outside of AgriProve's control. Returning all ACCUs includes returning AgriProves 25% as well. This means you would probably need to purchase ACCUs from the market. Why do you have to give back AgriProve's 25% as well? Think about it this way. Let's assume you were instead AgriProve money per hour to conduct work on your project. Then, 15 years later, you decide to terminate the project. It would not be reasonable to ask AgriProve to give you back all the money you had paid us for the our services over the last 15 years, just because you didn't want to do it anymore. The solution - dormancy: With AgriProve being proponent, it is our responsibility to maintain all project compliance obligations at our cost (Clause's 8.2.2, 9.1, 15.3). Under clause 15.1 the Operator (you) "may cease active implementation of Eligible Management Activities during the Term by issuing written notice to Project Proponent." I wanted to personally reach out, as I found your email on the Droughtmaster website and thought you might be interested to hear that Queensland producers Karen and Rob Scanlan, used their Droughtmaster herd to generate soil carbon credits. Their story here.: https://agriprove.io/fysh-cp-cs Using grazing management and pasture improvements they saw a massive 400% lift in carry capacity and earned 3,559 credits valued at over $124,000 at current ACCU price. Talk about the perfect management of a versatile breed that delivered straight to their bottom-line. I wanted to personally reach out, as I found your email on the Droughtmaster website and thought you might be interested to hear that Queensland producers Karen and Rob Scanlan, used their Droughtmaster herd to generate soil carbon credits. engagements.subject: AgriProve - soil carbon core density options
engagements.body: Hi Geoff and Lyndal, The team have finalised all the documentation required to issue you the Sales and Licence Agreement document package. Prior to issuing, we have several core sampling densities options. Please note that the depending on the size of the strata, the density will vary and as such, the below density numbers are an average across the projects. Please indicate what sampling density and associated cost you would like applied to your Sales and Licence Agreement from the below: Our recommendation targets a core density that aims to achieve a high confidence interval on sampling variance between cores for carbon levels, while taking into consideration the cost to landholders. Below this core density, variance may be greater and the confidence interval reduced, adversely affecting calculations. Above this density, there may be diminishing beneficial returns for sampling variance and increased costs. I have attached the draft sampling plans maps for your reference. You will see these have indicative core sampling points. Please note that these are examples only and are not finalised until prior to baseline sampling with a randomly generated seed number. Once confirmed, I will have the document package to you shortly following. I look forward to hearing from you! engagements.subject: Eligible Interest Holder Consent
engagements.body: Hi Geoff, Please see list of documents that we would typically send to the banks for them to assess and consent to carbon projects. As part of this process, we are required to obtain Eligible Interest Holder Consent from all parties who have an eligible interest on the land on which the project is located. This extends to financial institutions that have mortgages reflected on title for the project areas. We typically supply the EIH-Consent form required by the CER (pre-filled with project information) to the banks, along with the documents listed below that assists them in making their assessments/consenting. These documents are: – Eligible Interest Holder consent form required for signature – S27 declaration for the registration of an eligible offsets project (once project is declared) – AgriProve Sales and Licence Agreement: Key Commercial Terms, AgriProve Master Terms and Conditions, and AgriProve Standard Attachments – AgriProve Land Management Strategy and Carbon Project Plan – A Project Summary of the Carbon project with goals, management actions/activities and benefits As always, please reach out anytime you need. engagements.subject: Re: Contract
engagements.body: Hi Geoff and Lyndal, Thank you for your email. Please see my responses below to the questions raised yesterday on the phone and in your follow up email, with direct reference to the Key Commercial Terms and Master Terms (attached). AgriProve success fee. As detailed in the "AgriProve Remuneration" section on page 5 of the Key Commercial Terms, AgriProve Fee for this contract is 25% of all Project ACCUs and Project Co-benefits (for more on co-benefits refer to 9.2 of the Master Terms). Market Adjustment of AgriProve Fee states "Where this Market Offer Price is less than the AgriProve Fee under this Agreement, the AgriProve Fee will be reduced to the Market Offer". This means should the AgriProve Fee decrease, you will get the benefit of this under your contract. You are signing this contract with the understanding of a 25% AgriProve Fee, which cannot be arbitrarily increased, with the contract strictly omitting any ability to do so This is further controlled for by Clause 21 of the Master Terms and Conditions stating "AgriProve may amend the Master T&Cs from time to time... provided any amendments have no material adverse effect on Landholder or Operator". Sale of ACCUs through AgriProve as broker. AgriProve can help broker the sale of ACCUs for you, however, you are able to broker your own transaction without AgriProve acting as broker. No where in the contract are you bound to using AgriProve in brokering your ACCU transactions. If you choose to hold your own ACCUs, clause 8.2 of the Master T's & C's states AgriProve must transfer Project ACCUs to the Registry Account (Australian National Registry of Emissions Units (ANREU)) of the parties who are entitled to those project ACCUs. Please note that while it is not part of our obligations under the contract, AgriProve can assist you in setting up your own ANREU account. Partnering producers typically select Standard Option 2 or 3 on page 6 of the Key Commercial Terms as they are re-negotiable at anytime. Once your ANREU account is set up (typically this is done once we have measured an increase), we can switch to the distribution of your ACCUs to your ANREU account. For clarity, there are two mentions of brokerage in the Master T's and C's. The first is clause 11.4 which states in the event that Option 2 or Option 3 is pursued there is a brokerage fee. The second is clause 12.3 stating that the funds of the sales we broker must be transferred to you in 2 Business days (less brokerage). Default and Termination Yes, termination by the Operator will mean transferring to AgriProve the number of ACCU's issued to date. This is explained in clause 14.3.3 of the Master T's & C's. AgriProve will then give these all back to the regulator (we don't keep them) and terminate the project. To further explain; the soil carbon methodology requires projects to be monitored for 25 years. If you (the operator) choose to terminate the project prior to 25 years, the methodology requires all issued ACCUs to be returned, and this is outside of AgriProve's control. Returning all ACCUs includes returning AgriProves 25% as well. This means you would probably need to purchase ACCUs from the market. Why do you have to give back AgriProve's 25% as well? Think about it this way. Let's assume you were instead AgriProve money per hour to conduct work on your project. Then, 15 years later, you decide to terminate the project. It would not be reasonable to ask AgriProve to give you back all the money you had paid us for the our services over the last 15 years, just because you didn't want to do it anymore. The solution - dormancy: With AgriProve being proponent, it is our responsibility to maintain all project compliance obligations at our cost (Clause's 8.2.2, 9.1, 15.3). Under clause 15.1 the Operator (you) "may cease active implementation of Eligible Management Activities during the Term by issuing written notice to Project Proponent." Under clause 15.3 the Project Proponent (AgriProve) "will ensure that repor…

engagements.subject: Why Southern Queensland is Australia's carbon capital
engagements.body: G'Day Graham and Sharron, Ben from AgriProve here. I wanted to personally reach out because you're farming in what is objectively Australia's most productive region for soil carbon projects and I thought you should know why that matters for your bottom line. Let's talk about the Southern Queensland soil profile: Southern Queensland sits in the sweet spot for ideal soil profiles, resulting in soil carbon sequestration. Vertosols, Dermosols and Chromosol soil types can sequester higher than average carbon stocks that translates directly to potential ACCUs (Australian Carbon Credit Units) per hectare. If your farm is over 400 hectares and you want to chat further, feel free to call me on+61 483 921 562 , or do you have a time this week and would like to book in for a quick chat? See my link below. engagements.body: Graham and Sharron, Final time I'll personally reach out (promise). engagements.subject: Why Southern Queensland is Australia's carbon capital
engagements.body: G'Day Lauren, Ben from AgriProve here. I wanted to personally reach out because you're farming in what is objectively Australia's most productive region for soil carbon projects and I thought you should know why that matters for your bottom line. Let's talk about the Southern Queensland soil profile: Southern Queensland sits in the sweet spot for ideal soil profiles, resulting in soil carbon sequestration. engagements.subject: Why Central Queensland Coastal region is Australia's carbon capital
engagements.body: G'Day Val, Ben from AgriProve here. I wanted to personally reach out because, as a business dedicated to working extensively across the Central Queensland Coast, and I thought you might be interested in what we're seeing happen right across the region. Let's talk about the Central Queensland Coast soil profile: Central Queensland Coast is one of the most underrated soil carbon opportunities in Australia. With diverse soil types including Dermosols, Vertosols and Sodosol spanning from the coastal strip right through to the inland brigalow country, this translates directly to potential ACCUs (Australian Carbon Credit Units) per hectare. engagements.subject: MLA Field Day at Boreelum -  Steak and Wood - Wednesday 28th of May 2025 8:30am -3:00pm
engagements.body: Hi Amanda & Roger, AgriProve and Coffey Cattle Co would like to invite you to a FREE field day to learn all about how owners Adam and Jacynta combine tree growing with livestock grazing on their 2500-hectare property in Central Queensland. Discover how integrating trees and cattle on farm can lead to a more productive, profitable, and sustainable future for your business. This event is part of the Steak n Wood project, and will be showcasing the research being conducted by MLA in collaboration with Adam and Jac Coffey. Information and registration provided in this link: http://Head along for a FREE field day at Coffey Cattle Co. to learn all about how owners Adam and Jacynta combine tree growing with livestock grazing on their 2500-hectare property in Central Queensland. Discover how integrating trees and cattle on farm can lead to a more productive, profitable, and sustainable future for your business. This event is part of the Steak n Wood project, and will be showcasing the research being conducted by MLA in collaboration with Adam and Jac Coffey. engagements.subject: Why Central Queensland Coastal region is Australia's carbon capital
engagements.body: G'Day Ryan, Ben from AgriProve here. I wanted to personally reach out because, as a business dedicated to working extensively across the Central Queensland Coast, and I thought you might be interested in what we're seeing happen right across the region. Let's talk about the Central Queensland Coast soil profile: Central Queensland Coast is one of the most underrated soil carbon opportunities in Australia. engagements.subject: MLA Field Day at Boreelum -  Steak and Wood - Wednesday 28th of May 2025 8:30am -3:00pm
engagements.body: Hi Tony, AgriProve and Coffey Cattle Co would like to invite you to a FREE field day to learn all about how owners Adam and Jacynta combine tree growing with livestock grazing on their 2500-hectare property in Central Queensland. Discover how integrating trees and cattle on farm can lead to a more productive, profitable, and sustainable future for your business. This event is part of the Steak n Wood project, and will be showcasing the research being conducted by MLA in collaboration with Adam and Jac Coffey. Information and registration provided in this link: http://Head along for a FREE field day at Coffey Cattle Co. to learn all about how owners Adam and Jacynta combine tree growing with livestock grazing on their 2500-hectare property in Central Queensland. Discover how integrating trees and cattle on farm can lead to a more productive, profitable, and sustainable future for your business. This event is part of the Steak n Wood project, and will be showcasing the research being conducted by MLA in collaboration with Adam and Jac Coffey. The focus will be on: Inspect silvopastoral systems demonstration sites incorporating trees on farm with single and mixture hardwood species; a native forest silvopastoral system that has been sustainable managed to increase tree, pasture and livestock growth rates See the preliminary trial results and learn about the successes and challenges Discuss the multiple benefits of silvopastoral systems Financial outcome of these systems and more! We look forward to sharing the Coffey's story with you at 913 Bariveloe Road, Colosseum QLD on Wednesday the 28th of May from 8:30am - 3:00pm. engagements.subject: Why Southern Queensland is Australia's carbon capital
engagements.body: G'Day Tony, Ben from AgriProve here. engagements.subject: Why Central Queensland Coastal region is Australia's carbon capital
engagements.body: G'Day Jesse, Ben from AgriProve here. I wanted to personally reach out because, as a business dedicated to working extensively across the Central Queensland Coast, and I thought you might be interested in what we're seeing happen right across the region. Let's talk about the Central Queensland Coast soil profile: Central Queensland Coast is one of the most underrated soil carbon opportunities in Australia. engagements.subject: Why Central Queensland Coastal region is Australia's carbon capital
engagements.body: G'Day Rosemary & William, Ben from AgriProve here. engagements.body: Hi AW, AgriProve and Coffey Cattle Co would like to invite you to a FREE field day to learn all about how owners Adam and Jacynta combine tree growing with livestock grazing on their 2500-hectare property in Central Queensland. Discover how integrating trees and cattle on farm can lead to a more productive, profitable, and sustainable future for your business. This event is part of the Steak n Wood project, and will be showcasing the research being conducted by MLA in collaboration with Adam and Jac Coffey. Information and registration provided in this link: http://Head along for a FREE field day at Coffey Cattle Co. to learn all about how owners Adam and Jacynta combine tree growing with livestock grazing on their 2500-hectare property in Central Queensland. Discover how integrating trees and cattle on farm can lead to a more productive, profitable, and sustainable future for your business. This event is part of the Steak n Wood project, and will be showcasing the research being conducted by MLA in collaboration with Adam and Jac Coffey. engagements.subject: Why Central Queensland Coastal region is Australia's carbon capital
engagements.body: G'Day AW, Ben from AgriProve here. I wanted to personally reach out because, as a business dedicated to working extensively across the Central Queensland Coast, and I thought you might be interested in what we're seeing happen right across the region. Let's talk about the Central Queensland Coast soil profile: Central Queensland Coast is one of the most underrated soil carbon opportunities in Australia. engagements.subject: MLA Field Day at Boreelum -  Steak and Wood - Wednesday 28th of May 2025 8:30am -3:00pm
engagements.body: Hi Cliff, AgriProve and Coffey Cattle Co would like to invite you to a FREE field day to learn all about how owners Adam and Jacynta combine tree growing with livestock grazing on their 2500-hectare property in Central Queensland. Discover how integrating trees and cattle on farm can lead to a more productive, profitable, and sustainable future for your business. This event is part of the Steak n Wood project, and will be showcasing the research being conducted by MLA in collaboration with Adam and Jac Coffey. Information and registration provided in this link: http://Head along for a FREE field day at Coffey Cattle Co. to learn all about how owners Adam and Jacynta combine tree growing with livestock grazing on their 2500-hectare property in Central Queensland. Discover how integrating trees and cattle on farm can lead to a more productive, profitable, and sustainable future for your business. This event is part of the Steak n Wood project, and will be showcasing the research being conducted by MLA in collaboration with Adam and Jac Coffey. The focus will be on: Inspect silvopastoral systems demonstration sites incorporating trees on farm with single and mixture hardwood species; a native forest silvopastoral system that has been sustainable managed to increase tree, pasture and livestock growth rates See the preliminary trial results and learn about the successes and challenges Discuss the multiple benefits of silvopastoral systems Financial outcome of these systems and more! engagements.subject: Why Central Queensland Coastal region is Australia's carbon capital

I wanted to personally reach out because, as a business dedicated to working extensively across the Central Queensland Coast, and I thought you might be interested in what we're seeing happen right across the region. engagements.subject: How a Southern Queensland farmer achieved positive results with AgriProve
engagements.body: Libby, Final time I'll personally reach out (promise). I couldn't miss the opportunity to tell you about another farmer based in the Southern Queensland region doing something pretty remarkable. The Smith Carbon Project, located in the Darling Downs, has recently been issued 1,362 Australian Carbon Credit Units (ACCUs) You can read the full case study here: 👉The Smith Carbon Project Case Study: https://agriprove.io/smith-cp-cs1 The project has returned positive carbon sequestration by implementing key practices including: - Multi-species pasture and have increased the diversity of microbial. - Watering points and fencing were installed to support the subdivision of their land into smaller paddocks, increasing rotational grazing intensity. engagements.subject: Queensland Droughtmaster member lands soil carbon credits
engagements.body: Hi Sasha, Bill from AgriProve here. I wanted to personally reach out, as I found your email on the Droughtmaster website and thought you might be interested to hear that Queensland producers Karen and Rob Scanlan, used their Droughtmaster herd to generate soil carbon credits. Their story here.: https://agriprove.io/fysh-cp-cs Using grazing management and pasture improvements they saw a massive 400% lift in carry capacity and earned 3,559 credits valued at over $124,000 at current ACCU price. Talk about the perfect management of a versatile breed that delivered straight to their bottom-line. engagements.subject: MLA Field Day at Boreelum -  Steak and Wood - Wednesday 28th of May 2025 8:30am -3:00pm
engagements.body: Hi Sasha, AgriProve and Coffey Cattle Co would like to invite you to a FREE field day to learn all about how owners Adam and Jacynta combine tree growing with livestock grazing on their 2500-hectare property in Central Queensland. Discover how integrating trees and cattle on farm can lead to a more productive, profitable, and sustainable future for your business. This event is part of the Steak n Wood project, and will be showcasing the research being conducted by MLA in collaboration with Adam and Jac Coffey. Information and registration provided in this link: http://Head along for a FREE field day at Coffey Cattle Co. to learn all about how owners Adam and Jacynta combine tree growing with livestock grazing on their 2500-hectare property in Central Queensland. Discover how integrating trees and cattle on farm can lead to a more productive, profitable, and sustainable future for your business. This event is part of the Steak n Wood project, and will be showcasing the research being conducted by MLA in collaboration with Adam and Jac Coffey. The focus will be on: Inspect silvopastoral systems demonstration sites incorporating trees on farm with single and mixture hardwood species; a native forest silvopastoral system that has been sustainable managed to increase tree, pasture and livestock growth rates See the preliminary trial results and learn about the successes and challenges Discuss the multiple benefits of silvopastoral systems Financial outcome of these systems and more! We look forward to sharing the Coffey's story with you at 913 Bariveloe Road, Colosseum QLD on Wednesday the 28th of May from 8:30am - 3:00pm. engagements.subject: Why Central Queensland Coastal region is Australia's carbon capital
engagements.body: G'Day Sasha, Ben from AgriProve here. I wanted to personally reach out because, as a business dedicated to working extensively across the Central Queensland Coast, and I thought you might be interested in what we're seeing happen right across the region. engagements.subject: MLA Field Day at Boreelum -  Steak and Wood - Wednesday 28th of May 2025 8:30am -3:00pm
engagements.body: Hi Stanley, AgriProve and Coffey Cattle Co would like to invite you to a FREE field day to learn all about how owners Adam and Jacynta combine tree growing with livestock grazing on their 2500-hectare property in Central Queensland. Discover how integrating trees and cattle on farm can lead to a more productive, profitable, and sustainable future for your business. This event is part of the Steak n Wood project, and will be showcasing the research being conducted by MLA in collaboration with Adam and Jac Coffey. Information and registration provided in this link: http://Head along for a FREE field day at Coffey Cattle Co. to learn all about how owners Adam and Jacynta combine tree growing with livestock grazing on their 2500-hectare property in Central Queensland. Discover how integrating trees and cattle on farm can lead to a more productive, profitable, and sustainable future for your business. This event is part of the Steak n Wood project, and will be showcasing the research being conducted by MLA in collaboration with Adam and Jac Coffey. The focus will be on: Inspect silvopastoral systems demonstration sites incorporating trees on farm with single and mixture hardwood species; a native forest silvopastoral system that has been sustainable managed to increase tree, pasture and livestock growth rates See the preliminary trial results and learn about the successes and challenges Discuss the multiple benefits of silvopastoral systems Financial outcome of these systems and more! We look forward to sharing the Coffey's story with you at 913 Bariveloe Road, Colosseum QLD on Wednesday the 28th of May from 8:30am - 3:00pm. engagements.subject: Why Southern Queensland is Australia's carbon capital
engagements.body: G'Day Amy, Ben from AgriProve here. I wanted to personally reach out because you're farming in what is objectively Australia's most productive region for soil carbon projects and I thought you should know why that matters for your bottom line. Let's talk about the Southern Queensland soil profile: Southern Queensland sits in the sweet spot for ideal soil profiles, resulting in soil carbon sequestration. engagements.subject: How a Southern Queensland farmer achieved positive results with AgriProve
engagements.body: Amy, Final time I'll personally reach out (promise). I couldn't miss the opportunity to tell you about another farmer based in the Southern Queensland region doing something pretty remarkable. The Smith Carbon Project, located in the Darling Downs, has recently been issued 1,362 Australian Carbon Credit Units (ACCUs) You can read the full case study here: 👉The Smith Carbon Project Case Study: https://agriprove.io/smith-cp-cs1 The project has returned positive carbon sequestration by implementing key practices including: - Multi-species pasture and have increased the diversity of microbial. - Watering points and fencing were installed to support the subdivision of their land into smaller paddocks, increasing rotational grazing intensity. engagements.subject: Why Southern Queensland is Australia's carbon capital
engagements.body: G'Day Val, Ben from AgriProve here. I wanted to personally reach out because you're farming in what is objectively Australia's most productive region for soil carbon projects and I thought you should know why that matters for your bottom line. Let's talk about the Southern Queensland soil profile: Southern Queensland sits in the sweet spot for ideal soil profiles, resulting in soil carbon sequestration. Vertosols, Dermosols and Chromosol soil types can sequester higher than average carbon stocks that translates directly to potential ACCUs (Australian Carbon Credit Units) per hectare. If your farm is over 400 hectares and you want to chat further, feel free to call me on+61 483 921 562 , or do you have a time this week and would like to book in for a quick chat? See my link below. engagements.subject: Engagement document for signature
engagements.body: Hi Dale, ​Thank you for taking the time to complete the engagement documents with me. I look forward to getting your project scoping underway. To get started please review, sign and return the Consent to Register - Commitment to Implement form. I have also attached our Land Management Strategy that accompanies all AgriProve projects detailing how your project(s) are managed and monitored by AgriProve while ensuring our landholders maintain full management autonomy. A land management strategy is required by the Clean Energy Regulator for all Carbon Projects registered with them. Once returned, you’ll be assigned a dedicated Soil Carbon Project Officer and we will begin our project scoping process by: 1. Verifying your Land titles 2. Defining the soil carbon project area(s) - we will need to exclude areas that we cannot physically sample such as roads, dams, heavily timbered areas and other infrastructure 3. Designing project structure - based on operation type, land characteristics, and soil type. We employ a variety of technologies to do this. Our recommendations aim to maximise project success and ACCU yield. 4. Provide a quote on soil baseline sampling (your only project fee). 5. Provision you with our Sales and Licence Agreement to move forward. Once complete, you’ll have clarity of what’s involved when working with AgriProve on your soil carbon journey. I look forward to working with you further and congratulation on getting started. Dylan and I will work closely with you to finalise the details of your project, including: Land title verification Defining the soil carbon project area - we will need to exclude areas that we cannot physically sample such as roads, dams, heavily treed areas, and other infrastructure. Designing your project - based on operation type, land characteristics, and soil type. We employ a variety of technologies to do this. Our recommendations aim to maximise project success and ACCU yield. Provisioning of your final soil baseline sampling quote (your only project fee) and AgriProve’s Sales and Licence Agreement. We can expect this process to take about 2 weeks and will require some confirmations along the way and some time for a video meeting. Action item: Did you have some time Thursday or Friday (Friday preferrable for us) this week to meeting with Dylan and I for a project mapping alignment meeting? If so, do you have a couple of times that would suit you best? Thank you again for choosing AgriProve as your trusted carbon partner, and we look forward to supporting you on your journey. As always you can reach out with any questions. However, to provide you the answer now, Clause 15 of the Master Terms and Conditions states the operator (you) may cease active implementation of Eligible Management Activities during the Term by issuing written notice to Project Proponent (AgriProve). engagements.body: AgriProve Project Proposal Playbook Please provide a brief history of your farm 'Mulligans' property was purchased and settled September 2024. Under prior management this property had very little invested into system improvements having been run the same way for over 30 years. There has been no irrigation set up, no infrastructure improvements or pasture improvements and stock management has been minimal. Please provide a brief description of your background, any relevant accreditations, skills and experience and any ongoing training that assist in managing the land: Management expertise includes a lifetime of Agricultural experience with Dale coming from a family farm running sheep, having worked as farm hand across many cattle properties and owning and managing two different properties in Yepoon within the last decade prior to this purchase. Additionally, the farm hand employed has a Bachelor of Ag science and Jackie has bachelor of business and accounting, with this knowledge employed to ensure the best outcomes with a sustainable long-term outlook. Do you use any farm management software or digital tools? Or do you have any plans to implement any additional solutions to assist with record keeping? No, just notebook. Will start to implement herd movement recording using grazing chart. Will consider Tags for Tonnes, use of optiweigh and other software programs, including data available through an AgriProve project. Do you use any predictive modelling to assist in management decisions? No Do you currently have a detailed farm map including paddock mapping? Yes Notes: Requested Are you aware of any land clearing occurring: a.) In the past 7 years (if there has been no change in title ownership)? b.) In the past 5 years (if there has been change in title ownership )? No Are you aware of any wetlands being drained: a.) In the past 7 years (if there has been no change in title ownership)? b.) In the past 5 years (if there has been change in title ownership)? No Has the land been de-stocked for 2 consecutive years at any time during the past 5 years for non-approved purpose ? No Is there any evidence that suggests treed areas have been thinned for non-approved purposes ? No Are you aware of any land management activities in the last 5 years that involve the addition or redistribution of soil? No Do you have any plans to change land use through construction, building or irrigation? No Notes: Dale is no longer looking to irrigate after speaking with locals and his agronomist as it isn't practical in the area. It is high rainfall and by time it would be useful to irrigate in a drought there is typically restrictions on pumping form the river during these times. The following is no longer a relevant part of Dale's plan: Irrigation may take place on lot 1 and 39 0f plan 753512 in the future few years. No current infrastructure is set up for this and timeframes are not certain. Course of action will be to design project with 4 strata across the 160Ha project area. One of these strata will be on the lots eligible for irrigation. Then should these area's need to be varied out for irrigation we can make them exclusions and re-calculate baseline. Still having the minimum required strata number of 3. This decision takes into account that the titles qualify now as eligible, so we will keep them in the project in case the method changes (Soil Carbon Method is about to undergo review with irrigation restriction having been an issue raised). Give ourselves some flexibility as Dale won't irrigation for at least a couple of years and the titles haven't been irrigated for the last 5 years. 1. Are you applying synthetic or non-synthetic fertilisers to fix any nutrient shortage. Please specify which shortages were you addressing? What nutrient(s) are you currently addressing, and what product or range of products are you using to target this? If no specific nutrient is identified, what purpose do these products serve? engagements.subject: Queensland Droughtmaster member lands soil carbon credits
engagements.body: Hi Geraldine, Bill from AgriProve here. I wanted to personally reach out, as I found your email on the Droughtmaster website and thought you might be interested to hear that Queensland producers Karen and Rob Scanlan, used their Droughtmaster herd to generate soil carbon credits. Their story here.: https://agriprove.io/fysh-cp-cs Using grazing management and pasture improvements they saw a massive 400% lift in carry capacity and earned 3,559 credits valued at over $124,000 at current ACCU price. engagements.subject: Why Southern Queensland is Australia's carbon capital
engagements.body: G'Day Geraldine, Ben from AgriProve here. I wanted to personally reach out because you're farming in what is objectively Australia's most productive region for soil carbon projects and I thought you should know why that matters for your bottom line. Let's talk about the Southern Queensland soil profile: Southern Queensland sits in the sweet spot for ideal soil profiles, resulting in soil carbon sequestration. Vertosols, Dermosols and Chromosol soil types can sequester higher than average carbon stocks that translates directly to potential ACCUs (Australian Carbon Credit Units) per hectare. engagements.subject: AgriProve - soil carbon core density options
engagements.body: Hi Geoff and Lyndal, The team have finalised all the documentation required to issue you the Sales and Licence Agreement document package. Prior to issuing, we have several core sampling densities options. Please note that the depending on the size of the strata, the density will vary and as such, the below density numbers are an average across the projects. Please indicate what sampling density and associated cost you would like applied to your Sales and Licence Agreement from the below: Our recommendation targets a core density that aims to achieve a high confidence interval on sampling variance between cores for carbon levels, while taking into consideration the cost to landholders. Below this core density, variance may be greater and the confidence interval reduced, adversely affecting calculations. Above this density, there may be diminishing beneficial returns for sampling variance and increased costs. I have attached the draft sampling plans maps for your reference. You will see these have indicative core sampling points. Please note that these are examples only and are not finalised until prior to baseline sampling with a randomly generated seed number. Once confirmed, I will have the document package to you shortly following. I look forward to hearing from you! engagements.subject: Re: Contract
engagements.body: Hi Geoff and Lyndal, Thank you for your email. Please see my responses below to the questions raised yesterday on the phone and in your follow up email, with direct reference to the Key Commercial Terms and Master Terms (attached). AgriProve success fee. As detailed in the "AgriProve Remuneration" section on page 5 of the Key Commercial Terms, AgriProve Fee for this contract is 25% of all Project ACCUs and Project Co-benefits (for more on co-benefits refer to 9.2 of the Master Terms). Market Adjustment of AgriProve Fee states "Where this Market Offer Price is less than the AgriProve Fee under this Agreement, the AgriProve Fee will be reduced to the Market Offer". This means should the AgriProve Fee decrease, you will get the benefit of this under your contract. You are signing this contract with the understanding of a 25% AgriProve Fee, which cannot be arbitrarily increased, with the contract strictly omitting any ability to do so This is further controlled for by Clause 21 of the Master Terms and Conditions stating "AgriProve may amend the Master T&Cs from time to time... provided any amendments have no material adverse effect on Landholder or Operator". Sale of ACCUs through AgriProve as broker. AgriProve can help broker the sale of ACCUs for you, however, you are able to broker your own transaction without AgriProve acting as broker. No where in the contract are you bound to using AgriProve in brokering your ACCU transactions. If you choose to hold your own ACCUs, clause 8.2 of the Master T's & C's states AgriProve must transfer Project ACCUs to the Registry Account (Australian National Registry of Emissions Units (ANREU)) of the parties who are entitled to those project ACCUs. Please note that while it is not part of our obligations under the contract, AgriProve can assist you in setting up your own ANREU account. Partnering producers typically select Standard Option 2 or 3 on page 6 of the Key Commercial Terms as they are re-negotiable at anytime. Once your ANREU account is set up (typically this is done once we have measured an increase), we can switch to the distribution of your ACCUs to your ANREU account. For clarity, there are two mentions of brokerage in the Master T's and C's. The first is clause 11.4 which states in the event that Option 2 or Option 3 is pursued there is a brokerage fee. The second is clause 12.3 stating that the funds of the sales we broker must be transferred to you in 2 Business days (less brokerage). Default and Termination Yes, termination by the Operator will mean transferring to AgriProve the number of ACCU's issued to date. This is explained in clause 14.3.3 of the Master T's & C's. AgriProve will then give these all back to the regulator (we don't keep them) and terminate the project. To further explain; the soil carbon methodology requires projects to be monitored for 25 years. If you (the operator) choose to terminate the project prior to 25 years, the methodology requires all issued ACCUs to be returned, and this is outside of AgriProve's control. Returning all ACCUs includes returning AgriProves 25% as well. This means you would probably need to purchase ACCUs from the market. Why do you have to give back AgriProve's 25% as well? Think about it this way. Let's assume you were instead AgriProve money per hour to conduct work on your project. Then, 15 years later, you decide to terminate the project. It would not be reasonable to ask AgriProve to give you back all the money you had paid us for the our services over the last 15 years, just because you didn't want to do it anymore. The solution - dormancy: With AgriProve being proponent, it is our responsibility to maintain all project compliance obligations at our cost (Clause's 8.2.2, 9.1, 15.3). Under clause 15.1 the Operator (you) "may cease active implementation of Eligible Management Activities during the Term by issuing written notice to Project Proponent." Under clause 15.3 the Project Proponent (AgriProve) "will ensure that repor…

engagements.subject: Welcome To AgriProve, The Next Steps
engagements.body: Hi Dale​, Thank you very much for sending this through. It is great to have you onboard and we’re excited to be working with you on your carbon farming journey. I would like to introduce you to Dylan Jones, your Soil Carbon Project Co-Ordinator. Dylan and I will work closely with you to finalise the details of your project, including: Land title verification Defining the soil carbon project area - we will need to exclude areas that we cannot physically sample such as roads, dams, heavily treed areas, and other infrastructure. Designing your project - based on operation type, land characteristics, and soil type. We employ a variety of technologies to do this. Our recommendations aim to maximise project success and ACCU yield. Provisioning of your final soil baseline sampling quote (your only project fee) and AgriProve’s Sales and Licence Agreement. We can expect this process to take about 2 weeks and will require some confirmations along the way and some time for a video meeting. Action item: Did you have some time Thursday or Friday (Friday preferrable for us) this week to meeting with Dylan and I for a project mapping alignment meeting? If so, do you have a couple of times that would suit you best? Thank you again for choosing AgriProve as your trusted carbon partner, and we look forward to supporting you on your journey. As always you can reach out with any questions. engagements.body: Hi Dale, Great to speak with you just now. As discussed, Lot 1 and 39 will need to be excluded from project to avoid restrictions around the use of their irrigation licenses. We will also continue holding off until your name is processed onto the final few land titles. In the mean time, you can take a look at our FAQ's on the AgriProve website under Resources and help center: https://help.agriprove.io/. Of particular use will be: Can the contract be assigned or transferred to another party?: https://help.agriprove.io/the-agriprove-contract#Contract-assignment and What are the conditions under which the contract can be terminated?: https://help.agriprove.io/the-agriprove-contract#termination I have just realised that project dormancy is not answered which I will get the team to add in today. However, to provide you the answer now, Clause 15 of the Master Terms and Conditions states the operator (you) may cease active implementation of Eligible Management Activities during the Term by issuing written notice to Project Proponent (AgriProve). AgriProve will ensure that reporting obligations under the CFI Act are met (at our cost) and that the Carbon Project continues to remain a registered project under the ERF. You can commence active implementation whenever you would like. engagements.body: AgriProve Project Proposal Playbook Please provide a brief history of your farm 'Mulligans' property was purchased and settled September 2024. Under prior management this property had very little invested into system improvements having been run the same way for over 30 years. There has been no irrigation set up, no infrastructure improvements or pasture improvements and stock management has been minimal. Please provide a brief description of your background, any relevant accreditations, skills and experience and any ongoing training that assist in managing the land: Management expertise includes a lifetime of Agricultural experience with Dale coming from a family farm running sheep, having worked as farm hand across many cattle properties and owning and managing two different properties in Yepoon within the last decade prior to this purchase. Additionally, the farm hand employed has a Bachelor of Ag science and Jackie has bachelor of business and accounting, with this knowledge employed to ensure the best outcomes with a sustainable long-term outlook. Do you use any farm management software or digital tools? Or do you have any plans to implement any additional solutions to assist with record keeping? No, just notebook. Will start to implement herd movement recording using grazing chart. engagements.body: Hi Dale, ​Thank you for taking the time to complete the engagement documents with me. I look forward to getting your project scoping underway. To get started please review, sign and return the Consent to Register - Commitment to Implement form. I have also attached our Land Management Strategy that accompanies all AgriProve projects detailing how your project(s) are managed and monitored by AgriProve while ensuring our landholders maintain full management autonomy. A land management strategy is required by the Clean Energy Regulator for all Carbon Projects registered with them. Once returned, you’ll be assigned a dedicated Soil Carbon Project Officer and we will begin our project scoping process by: 1. Verifying your Land titles 2. Defining the soil carbon project area(s) - we will need to exclude areas that we cannot physically sample such as roads, dams, heavily timbered areas and other infrastructure 3. Designing project structure - based on operation type, land characteristics, and soil type. We employ a variety of technologies to do this. Our recommendations aim to maximise project success and ACCU yield. 4. Provide a quote on soil baseline sampling (your only project fee). 5. Provision you with our Sales and Licence Agreement to move forward. Once complete, you’ll have clarity of what’s involved when working with AgriProve on your soil carbon journey. engagements.body: AgriProve Project Proposal Playbook Please provide a brief history of your farm 'Mulligans' property was purchased and settled September 2024. Under prior management this property had very little invested into system improvements having been run the same way for over 30 years. There has been no irrigation set up, no infrastructure improvements or pasture improvements and stock management has been minimal. Please provide a brief description of your background, any relevant accreditations, skills and experience and any ongoing training that assist in managing the land: Management expertise includes a lifetime of Agricultural experience with Dale coming from a family farm running sheep, having worked as farm hand across many cattle properties and owning and managing two different properties in Yepoon within the last decade prior to this purchase. Additionally, the farm hand employed has a Bachelor of Ag science and Jackie has bachelor of business and accounting, with this knowledge employed to ensure the best outcomes with a sustainable long-term outlook. Do you use any farm management software or digital tools? Or do you have any plans to implement any additional solutions to assist with record keeping? No, just notebook. Will start to implement herd movement recording using grazing chart. Will consider Tags for Tonnes, use of optiweigh and other software programs, including data available through an AgriProve project. Do you use any predictive modelling to assist in management decisions? No Do you currently have a detailed farm map including paddock mapping? Yes Notes: Requested Are you aware of any land clearing occurring: a.) In the past 7 years (if there has been no change in title ownership)? b.) In the past 5 years (if there has been change in title ownership )? No Are you aware of any wetlands being drained: a.) In the past 7 years (if there has been no change in title ownership)? b.) In the past 5 years (if there has been change in title ownership)? No Has the land been de-stocked for 2 consecutive years at any time during the past 5 years for non-approved purpose ? No Is there any evidence that suggests treed areas have been thinned for non-approved purposes ? No Are you aware of any land management activities in the last 5 years that involve the addition or redistribution of soil? No Do you have any plans to change land use through construction, building or irrigation? No Notes: Dale is no longer looking to irrigate after speaking with locals and his agronomist as it isn't practical in the area. It is high rainfall and by time it would be useful to irrigate in a drought there is typically restrictions on pumping form the river during these times. The following is no longer a relevant part of Dale's plan: Irrigation may take place on lot 1 and 39 0f plan 753512 in the future few years. No current infrastructure is set up for this and timeframes are not certain. Course of action will be to design project with 4 strata across the 160Ha project area. One of these strata will be on the lots eligible for irrigation. Then should these area's need to be varied out for irrigation we can make them exclusions and re-calculate baseline. Still having the minimum required strata number of 3. This decision takes into account that the titles qualify now as eligible, so we will keep them in the project in case the method changes (Soil Carbon Method is about to undergo review with irrigation restriction having been an issue raised). Give ourselves some flexibility as Dale won't irrigation for at least a couple of years and the titles haven't been irrigated for the last 5 years. 1. engagements.body: AgriProve Project Proposal Playbook Please provide a brief history of your farm Purchased and settle property purchase in June 2024. Operating the property from March 2024. engagements.subject: Wannawong Carbon Project at Risk
engagements.body: Hi Tom, I just wanted to check in to see how you found the project proposal? Are looking to move forward with it? The reason for my continued follow ups is there are time sensitivities around eligible activities. If you implement the project activities this cropping season and have not registered and had the project declared, there will be additional complexities in showing the required on farm changes that must commence after the project has been declared. This could lead to more questions about the 'newness' component of eligible activities and increases the risk of credits not being awarded and workload required from you to show change to have ACCUs issued. AgriProve are experts in helping our farmers meet these requirements smoothly and without fuss, however we strongly suggest moving your project forward as quickly as possible to avoid additional complexities. Also, incase you missed it, take a look a the Felmingham family's cropping and carbon story: https://agriprove.io/fife-carbon-project which generated 5,435ACCUs valued at $190,000 in just over a year! engagements.body: AgriProve Project Proposal Playbook Please provide a brief history of your farm Mallawa station was purchased in the mid 2000's by Emma's family. Mallawa is 1 of 3 properties in the family business and is looking to be transferred to Emma and Brenton's name and management this year as part of succession. Mallawa has always a beef production property with no cropping. Historical management has been continuous set stocking with little to no rest periods or destocking to match declining feed availability. With the upcoming transition of management to Brenton and Emma, changes to property management will be implemented with a focus on soil health as foundational to better production and increased farm resilience. Please provide a brief description of your background, any relevant accreditations, skills and experience and any ongoing training that assist in managing the land: Emma has grown up on farm and is familiar with the farming system and environmental climate it operates in. With an Bachelors in Education, Emma has conducted extensive research of industry best practice alongside Brenton. Based on these learnings they will look to better align management with industry best practice for improving farm health and productivity. Brenton has done Grazing for Profit courses, Low stress stock handling courses and has 10+ years hands on experience working on Mallawa and is looking to implement these learnings in the operation upon management transition. Do you use any farm management software or digital tools? Or do you have any plans to implement any additional solutions to assist with record keeping? No current use of farm management software or digital tools. Will look to investigate and implement software on farm as well as utilize the digital tools available through a soil carbon project. Although there is an above ground power line that runs along the eastern boundary at top sullivans (yellow and orange) also we have applied grassland herbicide all the way along this boundary. engagements.subject: AgriProve as project proponent
engagements.body: Hi Brenton, I watned to follow up on our discussion about project proponent, as I understand the approach seems different to what producers would initially perceive as the risk adverse option, being proponent themselves. As it isn't intuitively obvious the reasons why landowners as proponent is potentially more risky, I want to take the time to explain the benefits of AgriProve as proponent in writing and stress that this has been done to reduce risk on the producer and increase uptake. AgriProve acting as proponent means we are responsible for regulatory compliance associated legal (civil and criminal) penalties for non-compliance, and reduces the regulatory and compliance risk to the landholder. It also means we are the primary contact point with the CER and allows us to handle these communications with our significant compliance expertise, reducing administrative burden on landowners. AgriProve as proponent affords flexibility of management to the landholder, with the ability to cease the active project implementation at any time. As proponent we then maintain the project administratively and ensure it remains compliant to avoid ACCU relinquishment. These administrative requirements would fall to a landholder as proponent for managing a non-active project. Risk associated with potential ACCU relinquishment requirements are borne by AgriProve where these relinquishment requirements are not due to a breach of our Master Terms and Conditions (such as complete termination of the project my the operator/landowner within the project 25 year permanence period) AgriProve acting as proponent provides a mechanism for sale of farm without terminating projects and requiring ACCUs to be relinquished - the project remains active with AgriProve and we have a vested interest in assisting with project agreement novation to new owners. Efficiency of start-up - we can get registrations lodged immediately. Landowner as proponent would need to get established with the CER before being able to register projects. This could add an additional 3 months to the process. I hope this helps clarify some of our conversation. As always, give be a bell if you have any questions. Speak soon. engagements.subject: AgriProve as project proponent
engagements.body: Hi Brenton, I watned to follow up on our discussion about project proponent, as I understand the approach seems different to what producers would initially perceive as the risk adverse option, being proponent themselves. As it isn't intuitively obvious the reasons why landowners as proponent is potentially more risky, I want to take the time to explain the benefits of AgriProve as proponent in writing and stress that this has been done to reduce risk on the producer and increase uptake. AgriProve acting as proponent means we are responsible for regulatory compliance associated legal (civil and criminal) penalties for non-compliance, and reduces the regulatory and compliance risk to the landholder. It also means we are the primary contact point with the CER and allows us to handle these communications with our significant compliance expertise, reducing administrative burden on landowners. AgriProve as proponent affords flexibility of management to the landholder, with the ability to cease the active project implementation at any time. As proponent we then maintain the project administratively and ensure it remains compliant to avoid ACCU relinquishment. These administrative requirements would fall to a landholder as proponent for managing a non-active project. Risk associated with potential ACCU relinquishment requirements are borne by AgriProve where these relinquishment requirements are not due to a breach of our Master Terms and Conditions (such as complete termination of the project my the operator/landowner within the project 25 year permanence period) AgriProve acting as proponent provides a mechanism for sale of farm without terminating projects and requiring ACCUs to be relinquished - the project remains active with AgriProve and we have a vested interest in assisting with project agreement novation to new owners. Efficiency of start-up - we can get registrations lodged immediately. Landowner as proponent would need to get established with the CER before being able to register projects. This could add an additional 3 months to the process. I hope this helps clarify some of our conversation. As always, give be a bell if you have any questions. Speak soon. engagements.subject: AgriProve as project proponent
engagements.body: Hi Brenton, I watned to follow up on our discussion about project proponent, as I understand the approach seems different to what producers would initially perceive as the risk adverse option, being proponent themselves. As it isn't intuitively obvious the reasons why landowners as proponent is potentially more risky, I want to take the time to explain the benefits of AgriProve as proponent in writing and stress that this has been done to reduce risk on the producer and increase uptake. AgriProve acting as proponent means we are responsible for regulatory compliance associated legal (civil and criminal) penalties for non-compliance, and reduces the regulatory and compliance risk to the landholder. It also means we are the primary contact point with the CER and allows us to handle these communications with our significant compliance expertise, reducing administrative burden on landowners. AgriProve as proponent affords flexibility of management to the landholder, with the ability to cease the active project implementation at any time. As proponent we then maintain the project administratively and ensure it remains compliant to avoid ACCU relinquishment. These administrative requirements would fall to a landholder as proponent for managing a non-active project. Risk associated with potential ACCU relinquishment requirements are borne by AgriProve where these relinquishment requirements are not due to a breach of our Master Terms and Conditions (such as complete termination of the project my the operator/landowner within the project 25 year permanence period) AgriProve acting as proponent provides a mechanism for sale of farm without terminating projects and requiring ACCUs to be relinquished - the project remains active with AgriProve and we have a vested interest in assisting with project agreement novation to new owners. Efficiency of start-up - we can get registrations lodged immediately. Landowner as proponent would need to get established with the CER before being able to register projects. This could add an additional 3 months to the process. I hope this helps clarify some of our conversation. As always, give be a bell if you have any questions. Speak soon. engagements.subject: Why Central Queensland Coastal region is Australia's carbon capital
engagements.body: G'Day Brenton, Ben from AgriProve here. I wanted to personally reach out because, as a business dedicated to working extensively across the Central Queensland Coast, and I thought you might be interested in what we're seeing happen right across the region. Let's talk about the Central Queensland Coast soil profile: Central Queensland Coast is one of the most underrated soil carbon opportunities in Australia. With diverse soil types including Dermosols, Vertosols and Sodosol spanning from the coastal strip right through to the inland brigalow country, this translates directly to potential ACCUs (Australian Carbon Credit Units) per hectare. engagements.subject: How a Southern Queensland farmer achieved positive results with AgriProve
engagements.body: Brenton, Final time I'll personally reach out (promise). I couldn't miss the opportunity to tell you about another farmer based in the Southern Queensland region doing something pretty remarkable. engagements.body: Hi Brenton, I watned to follow up on our discussion about project proponent, as I understand the approach seems different to what producers would initially perceive as the risk adverse option, being proponent themselves. As it isn't intuitively obvious the reasons why landowners as proponent is potentially more risky, I want to take the time to explain the benefits of AgriProve as proponent in writing and stress that this has been done to reduce risk on the producer and increase uptake. AgriProve acting as proponent means we are responsible for regulatory compliance associated legal (civil and criminal) penalties for non-compliance, and reduces the regulatory and compliance risk to the landholder. It also means we are the primary contact point with the CER and allows us to handle these communications with our significant compliance expertise, reducing administrative burden on landowners. AgriProve as proponent affords flexibility of management to the landholder, with the ability to cease the active project implementation at any time. As proponent we then maintain the project administratively and ensure it remains compliant to avoid ACCU relinquishment. These administrative requirements would fall to a landholder as proponent for managing a non-active project. Risk associated with potential ACCU relinquishment requirements are borne by AgriProve where these relinquishment requirements are not due to a breach of our Master Terms and Conditions (such as complete termination of the project my the operator/landowner within the project 25 year permanence period) AgriProve acting as proponent provides a mechanism for sale of farm without terminating projects and requiring ACCUs to be relinquished - the project remains active with AgriProve and we have a vested interest in assisting with project agreement novation to new owners. Efficiency of start-up - we can get registrations lodged immediately. Landowner as proponent would need to get established with the CER before being able to register projects. This could add an additional 3 months to the process. I hope this helps clarify some of our conversation. As always, give be a bell if you have any questions. Speak soon. engagements.subject: AgriProve as project proponent
engagements.body: Hi Brenton, I watned to follow up on our discussion about project proponent, as I understand the approach seems different to what producers would initially perceive as the risk adverse option, being proponent themselves. As it isn't intuitively obvious the reasons why landowners as proponent is potentially more risky, I want to take the time to explain the benefits of AgriProve as proponent in writing and stress that this has been done to reduce risk on the producer and increase uptake. AgriProve acting as proponent means we are responsible for regulatory compliance associated legal (civil and criminal) penalties for non-compliance, and reduces the regulatory and compliance risk to the landholder. It also means we are the primary contact point with the CER and allows us to handle these communications with our significant compliance expertise, reducing administrative burden on landowners. AgriProve as proponent affords flexibility of management to the landholder, with the ability to cease the active project implementation at any time. As proponent we then maintain the project administratively and ensure it remains compliant to avoid ACCU relinquishment. These administrative requirements would fall to a landholder as proponent for managing a non-active project. Risk associated with potential ACCU relinquishment requirements are borne by AgriProve where these relinquishment requirements are not due to a breach of our Master Terms and Conditions (such as complete termination of the project my the operator/landowner within the project 25 year permanence period) AgriProve acting as proponent provides a mechanism for sale of farm without terminating projects and requiring ACCUs to be relinquished - the project remains active with AgriProve and we have a vested interest in assisting with project agreement novation to new owners. Efficiency of start-up - we can get registrations lodged immediately. Landowner as proponent would need to get established with the CER before being able to register projects. This could add an additional 3 months to the process. I hope this helps clarify some of our conversation. As always, give be a bell if you have any questions. Speak soon. engagements.body: G'Day Brenton, Ben from AgriProve here. I wanted to personally reach out because, as a business dedicated to working extensively across the Central Queensland Coast, and I thought you might be interested in what we're seeing happen right across the region. Discovery call: "trying to understand what sort of kick to the balls he's had with frost damage to his crops" - 10-90% potential damage and crop loss depending on the crop. Canola, Barley, wheat etc. Tend to think they are getting a shift in climatic conditions affecting to his operation. Does subscribe to agronomy long-term forecasting tool to support his above view agronomist by trade Operation: Mixed enterprise - runs sheep and wants to run a few more to reduce risk from crop losses Mixed cropping operation Griffith based 4200 Ha Entire program including lease country 2900 Ha total Loam - 1000 Ha potentially "What does excite me about a soil carbon project is.... mallee soil type, which is inherently infertile but I am trying to improve it with management best practice through his farming and agronomy expertise" Original enquiry: At a minimum wanted to get baseline data, i.e. sampling done to support his management program. enquired with Loam Bio: has asked for a baseline quote Questions: not too sure about the new and materially different practice change - explained this in terms of regulator language and eligibility criteria Management practices / practice change - has introduced chicken production last 2 years - has introduced irrigation onto the farm Can irrigate about 756 Ha of his property and has done for the past 2 years Chicken manure is available to him and has been spreading recently - not sure how long Question: Prescribing to loambio seed coating: CSIRO trial - 2-year "these clever dudes" the thought of adding a fungus production seed coating has been questioned Scott doesn't want to prescribe to a management program with his carbon project Question - baseline costs Pretty happy with the ACCU share to cover future costs Doesn't have any baseline sampling data Wishes he did this 20 years ago Project configuration questions: has introduced irrigation in the past 2 years. - is this a flag for a soil carbon project? can Next steps: request lot and plan numbers scott@tabbitafarming.com.au

engagements.body: Hi Scott, As mentioned, I have received approval from Hone Ag for your property as part of the NSCIC. The National Soil Carbon Innovation Challenge (NSCIC) is a government-funded grant that subsidises your baselining fee and provides you with Hone's leading-edge tech. Hone's hand-held device measures soil organic carbon using near-infrared (NIR) spectroscopy. The challenge aims to build accuracy for in-field tech. The commitment on your end is to complete 30 scans per quarter, although there is no limit to the use of the Hone device. I've attached the relevant documents. As discussed over the phone, you'll have 30 soil cores (approx. 350 Ha) fully subsidised which equates to roughly $13,000 in baselining & access to the Hone Soil Carbon Device. Land and expand approach: It is worth mentioning how we structure a staggered project rollout. We would normally include the next 12-30 months of property area in the upfront registration application. This approach creates a soil carbon project in installments with no need for additional documentation / registration procedures with the regulator. We then split the projects based on your plan to implement for your farm management plan and spread the baseline sampling costs. Our next step is to identify the total area of the property you're interested in starting with and go from there. I'll call you later this arvo to walk through the options Cheers, Scott Scott Nevison | Business Development Manager Phone: 1300 GO SOIL Mobile: +61 483 904 941 / +61 450 276 079 Email: scott@agriprove.io Address: 1/601 Dean St, Albury NSW 2640 Here at AgriProve we care for your privacy. Check in call - drafting proposal: looking to purchase a disc seeder - this will be a tool that is new and materially different Need to understand the specific material difference compared to the past 5 years How has he managed the residual Tillage - by using a disc seeder don't need to What have you been doing to approach soil nutrient deficiency Grazing management over the residual crop - this alters stocking intensity Implementation of the project Any one of the above would be generally considered eligible, but the key is the material difference in approach. What you do to meet that material difference is up to you. The range of activities that fall under disc seeder Reduced tillage and stubble retention - if there is a material difference in how this has been done in the past 5 years. "Next logical extension" Altering stocking rate if sheep are now grazed more intensively on the crop residue "New logical extension" Approach for nutrient deficiency Move towards a new approach, i.e. introducing a new product is a material different Based on a carbon approach, that may seek to reduce synthetics for example New land management strategy will need further detail and specifics to satisfy the regulators requirements
