engagements.body: G’day Harrison, We have now finished harvest so I am in the midst of getting my office work into some semblance of order. The last correspondence from Scott was a bit of an impasse as I had suggested using a couple of irrigated fields and he said they came with some complications in terms of methodology. I had not responded to that email as I got busy with harvest. My irrigation infrastructure is all pivot irrigators and it covers an area of approximately 760ha. We also own 2,150ha of dry area & lease another 1,600ha of dry area. The pivots mean I can be precise with my irrigation application so that may help with methodology. Otherwise I am happy to work with you guys with some of the dry area – we purchased a new dry area block in 2023 (658ha which has approximately 410ha arable) and I think it would be the best one to baseline for improvement as it has had a very conventional farming history and our program is more aligned to no-till with the introduction of chook manure to help fertility. I am also excited about bringing the irrigation into a carbon project as I have only introduced the pivots onto the farm in the past 3-4 years & I think I can drive the accumulation of carbon hard with the strategic use of the pivots. Our business has an increasing focus on graze & grain opportunities using our sheep enterprise, but I am also putting more focus on pasture with a lucerne base and simply sowing grazing crop into that lucerne each year under a couple of the pivots. By the sounds of it though, the irrigation aspect may make it tricky for the methodology?? Thank you for the introduction, Harry. Hi Scott, Bill Hyem here, it is great to be introduced to the conversation and I look forward to helping alongside Harry with any questions you have, to get your journey started. It sounds like there is some great opportunity across the different cropping systems you run. It would be great to find some time for a 15-minute call to discuss some different scenarios we can start to consider, and to get you set up with some initial emissions and project potential estimates on our newly launched customer platform. Based on the information below I would agree that the newly acquired 410ha arable dryland block would be the best starting point given the change in management you will continue to implement and no irrigation restrictions. We can then discuss scaling project size to incorporate other dryland areas based on your current and future plans, costs etc. As you suggested, irrigated areas present a fantastic opportunity for soil carbon projects, and we would be excited to explore this opportunity with you. The methods restrictions are simple but important to consider and are as follows: For each 5-year block in the project lifespan the water application to the project area cannot exceed 20% higher than the average of the 5-years prior to starting the project (what is known as the Baseline Management Period). E.g. If your average irrigation over the past 5 years for the 760Ha of pivots has been 3000ML/Yr, the total would be 15,000ML over the 5 years. For each 5-year block in the project your irrigation total cannot exceed 18,000ML (20% higher than 15,000). Similarly, the irrigation applied to the area in any one project year must not exceed 20% more than the highest single irrigation year in the 5 years prior to starting the project (Baseline Management Period). E.g. If the highest single year irrigation amount for the area in the 5 years prior to starting the project was 4000ML, then the highest single year irrigation during the project cannot exceed 4800ML (20% higher than 4,000). Therefore, we suggest having completed 5 years of irrigation at a rate you are unlikely to need to exceed by 20% during the project lifetime for any 5-year block or any single year. This will ensure you are not restricted in your day-to-day operation. AgriProve’s process for project design, monitoring and measurement has been built to maximise flexibility and management on the farmers behalf, for circumstances such as this. We would work with you in our strategy meetings to design the most suitable project areas and rollout plan. It would be great to find some time for a 15-minute call or video meeting to discuss some different scenarios we can start to consider, and to get you set up with some initial emissions and project potential estimates on our newly launched customer platform. Do you have some time this week or next? Kind regards,

Grew up in Coonabaraban, familiar with Gunnedah (Keepit Dam), father was engineer with telstra, moved to Young as a result. Then agronomy brought him to Griffith. Soil Type: Mallee red brown loam sandy soil. Current management: Disc seeder system - full no till. Has already purchased disc seeder. Not used but will in April Supplementing the synthetic with more animal mature. Option to replace. Has used over last few years. Dryland paddock has had manure, application rate will increase from last year. Dryland was 2t/Ha, this year will do at 3t/Ha after starting project. Perennial understory with Canola or wheat for pivot area. This year first ever seen a legume since new management on new dryland block. Will continue to have legumes in rotation ongoing.

Eligible activity decision: Legume introduction. New and clear cut however a rotation only every 3 or so years will be restrictive to resample schedule. Adding in no till and increased chicken manure application. Both are materially different and slightly weak but together should constitute additionality. Use case: Probably wait until legume rotation for first re-sample round. However, if second resample was to occur prior to another legume crop we can still use the other activities to satisfy additionality.

AgriProve Project Proposal Playbook Please provide a brief history of your farm The Ranch has been in Jill's family since 1960's, with Scott working on farm for 24 years since 2000. The property has always been a mixed farming enterprise. Historically management focused on a cropping to fallow rotation (One year off, one on). Scott has slowly transitioned this system to a continual cropping program maintaining ground cover. An increased focus on mixed enterprise has seen sheep numbers increase over the last 6 years. There has also been an establishment of a perennial pastures (Lucerne). Property owned by Scott and Wife Jill (Primary school teacher), with management run by Scott. The current area considered for a project was purchased in 2022. History includes conventional cropping practices including small crop rotation, cultivation and fallow. Scott is steadily working on transition the system to management practices more suited to building healthy soils and a soil carbon project will help guide and incentivise this transition. Please provide a brief description of your background, any relevant accreditations, skills and experience and any ongoing training that assist in managing the land: Scott has a Bachelor of Applied Science in Agriculture, a Graduate Diploma in Vocational Education, which was actively used to teach cotton production and farm chemical use courses. Scott is also a trained Agronomist, with this background leading to employment with Twynum Pastoral Company as head agronomist for 2 years overseeing 3100Ha of cotton production annually. Also worked for DPI in Cotton institute development officer for Southern NSW for 2 years and as an Agribusiness consultant for 2 years. Management of The Ranch started in 2007 and took over operation fully 2016. Irrigation was introduced to certain areas of the property in 2021. Do you use any farm management software or digital tools? Or do you have any plans to implement any additional solutions to assist with record keeping? Tried Agworld, not enough value in it so stick to spreadsheets. Finding he is starting to use John Deere Ops Centre for field operation. No major plans outside this beyond what will be accessible through a project. Will continue to explore options. Do you use any predictive modelling to assist in management decisions? Yes, Ipaddock software (yields), keeps eye on rainfall records and give predictive yield based on your old yield data. Soil moisture monitoring interface and Mait Industry for irrigation management of pivots. Scott also uses Schedule-it moisture monitoring. 13 Moisture monitors strategically located across the farm to kept an eye on moisture level to inform management decisions. Do you currently have a detailed farm map including paddock mapping? Yes Notes: Yes, KMZ file provided and on file. Ensure pastured/treed areas are cut out of project completely (not just exclusion) as this may be put under project later. Are you aware of any land clearing occurring: a.) No Has the land been de-stocked for 2 consecutive years at any time during the past 5 years for non-approved purpose ? No Notes: N/A Is there any evidence that suggests treed areas have been thinned for non-approved purposes ? No Notes: N/A Are you aware of any land management activities in the last 5 years that involve the addition or redistribution of soil? Yes Notes: Laser bucketed some very shallow gullies so that they are trafficable by machinery, redistribution of top soils. engagements.subject: AgriProve - Process changes impacting projects registered after 8th November
engagements.body: Hi Tim and Courtney, I hope this message finds you well. I wanted to reach out to keep you informed of an important update that may impact your carbon project registration with AgriProve. The Clean Energy Regulator (CER) is updating some of their processes, and as a result, if we do not receive your sign agreement (Key Commercial Terms) by the 8th November we will need to revise your documentation to ensure we align with their requirements. This will mean additional paperwork for you, and we understand how valuable your time is. To avoid any unnecessary delays, we’re aiming to have all current agreements signed and finalised before 8th November. Please note that signing now does not lock you in to baselining immediately, and we will work with you to schedule sampling at a time that suits you. Invoicing for baselining only occurs after sampling has been completed and results are supplied to you. Our priority is making this as seamless as possible for you and ensuring that your project moves forward without extra hassle. We’re here to support you through this process and ensure that everything is handled smoothly and with your best interests in mind. I'll give you a call to makes sure you received my email and should you have any questions or need assistance, don’t hesitate to reach out. I am going to send him the FAQ's and organise that meeting to happen.

engagements.subject: AgriProve Follow up & Solicitor Details
engagements.body: Good Afternoon Tim, Great to chat to you today! Its a very small world. I checked up on a few of the things we spoke about and the answers are below: * As mentioned, there is a few ways out of the contract with that 5 year mark being a major one. Happy to meet your solicitor and go through that. * If AgriProve did go broke - you could transfer your project to another proponent. You would be able to take your sample results elsewhere and continue the project with someone else. This is because the main contract to get ACCUS is with the government, we are the people in the middle helping, but if we voided our end by going broke and not being able to continue you could go elsewhere. * Us being sold to a Chinese company - we cant predict that, but no matter what if someone bought us they would have to honor the project commitment to you as they would be buying the contracts with it. They couldn't take your ACCU's or have any claim on your land ect.- they would just be buying our part of it. * No matter what happens on our end your percentage of the ACCU's are yours. Here is the link for your solicitor to some of the commonly asked questions: https://help.agriprove.io/the-agriprove-contract Let us know and we can lock in a time with you and the solicitor to go through it all. Talk soon. they are using AG360 and are doing it often they have done Prograze, 3 day RCS clinic and the RCS Grazing for Profit Course. They have been applying pasture seed via air- mixed grass species with sub and arrow leaf clovers for legumes. (It is too steep to sow with a tractor). they have agronomist soil test done and they said the thing they needed was Sulfur. they have been applying elemental sulfur with the pasture seed- working through applying to whole place and are almost done. The intention is to get soil test done after the sulfur is done and find out what more they need. They used to use Superphosphate and are now only going to use natural products like the sulfur due to wanting to promote soil microbes. They are aiming for 50ha paddocks for now- will be fencing a big paddock in half to change grazing pressure and allow longer rest on other paddocks. Currently aim for 2 weeks per paddock, but make the decision based on the grass and season, always trying to leave 2-3 inches in the paddock and to maintain groundcover. 2 weeks across the current 6 paddocks is 12 weeks rest. Will plan to feed in a smaller area to protect grass if a drought happened to help maintain carbon too. Said he was never planning to go back to synthetic fertiliser is using legumes for nitrogen- planting the clovers and getting them established in the less fertile areas first, then planting the grass after as the nitrogen helps and have seen the grasses perform better when done this way rather than together.

engagements.body: Hi Tim and Courtney, I hope this message finds you well. I wanted to reach out to keep you informed of an important update that may impact your carbon project registration with AgriProve. The Clean Energy Regulator (CER) is updating some of their processes, and as a result, if we do not receive your sign agreement (Key Commercial Terms) by the 8th November we will need to revise your documentation to ensure we align with their requirements. This will mean additional paperwork for you, and we understand how valuable your time is. To avoid any unnecessary delays, we’re aiming to have all current agreements signed and finalised before 8th November. Please note that signing now does not lock you in to baselining immediately, and we will work with you to schedule sampling at a time that suits you. The 5 year out seemed like a good thing that he didnt know about and eased him a bit. Now interested in getting the ball moving again- starting with us talking to his solicitor. I am going to send him the FAQ's and organise that meeting to happen.

engagements.subject: AgriProve Follow up & Solicitor Details
engagements.body: Good Afternoon Tim, Great to chat to you today! Its a very small world. I checked up on a few of the things we spoke about and the answers are below: * As mentioned, there is a few ways out of the contract with that 5 year mark being a major one. Happy to meet your solicitor and go through that. * If AgriProve did go broke - you could transfer your project to another proponent. You would be able to take your sample results elsewhere and continue the project with someone else. This is because the main contract to get ACCUS is with the government, we are the people in the middle helping, but if we voided our end by going broke and not being able to continue you could go elsewhere. * Us being sold to a Chinese company - we cant predict that, but no matter what if someone bought us they would have to honor the project commitment to you as they would be buying the contracts with it. They couldn't take your ACCU's or have any claim on your land ect.- they would just be buying our part of it. * No matter what happens on our end your percentage of the ACCU's are yours. Here is the link for your solicitor to some of the commonly asked questions: https://help.agriprove.io/the-agriprove-contract Let us know and we can lock in a time with you and the solicitor to go through it all. Talk soon. they are using AG360 and are doing it often they have done Prograze, 3 day RCS clinic and the RCS Grazing for Profit Course. They have been applying pasture seed via air- mixed grass species with sub and arrow leaf clovers for legumes. (It is too steep to sow with a tractor). they have agronomist soil test done and they said the thing they needed was Sulfur. they have been applying elemental sulfur with the pasture seed- working through applying to whole place and are almost done. The intention is to get soil test done after the sulfur is done and find out what more they need. They used to use Superphosphate and are now only going to use natural products like the sulfur due to wanting to promote soil microbes. They are aiming for 50ha paddocks for now- will be fencing a big paddock in half to change grazing pressure and allow longer rest on other paddocks. Currently aim for 2 weeks per paddock, but make the decision based on the grass and season, always trying to leave 2-3 inches in the paddock and to maintain groundcover. 2 weeks across the current 6 paddocks is 12 weeks rest. Will plan to feed in a smaller area to protect grass if a drought happened to help maintain carbon too. Said he was never planning to go back to synthetic fertiliser is using legumes for nitrogen- planting the clovers and getting them established in the less fertile areas first, then planting the grass after as the nitrogen helps and have seen the grasses perform better when done this way rather than together.

engagements.body: Hi Tim and Courtney, I hope this message finds you well. I wanted to reach out to keep you informed of an important update that may impact your carbon project registration with AgriProve. The Clean Energy Regulator (CER) is updating some of their processes, and as a result, if we do not receive your sign agreement (Key Commercial Terms) by the 8th November we will need to revise your documentation to ensure we align with their requirements. This will mean additional paperwork for you, and we understand how valuable your time is. To avoid any unnecessary delays, we’re aiming to have all current agreements signed and finalised before 8th November. Please note that signing now does not lock you in to baselining immediately, and we will work with you to schedule sampling at a time that suits you. The 5 year out seemed like a good thing that he didnt know about and eased him a bit. Now interested in getting the ball moving again- starting with us talking to his solicitor. I am going to send him the FAQ's and organise that meeting to happen.

engagements.subject: AgriProve Follow up & Solicitor Details
engagements.body: Good Afternoon Tim, Great to chat to you today! Its a very small world. I checked up on a few of the things we spoke about and the answers are below: * As mentioned, there is a few ways out of the contract with that 5 year mark being a major one. Happy to meet your solicitor and go through that. * If AgriProve did go broke - you could transfer your project to another proponent. You would be able to take your sample results elsewhere and continue the project with someone else. This is because the main contract to get ACCUS is with the government, we are the people in the middle helping, but if we voided our end by going broke and not being able to continue you could go elsewhere. * Us being sold to a Chinese company - we cant predict that, but no matter what if someone bought us they would have to honor the project commitment to you as they would be buying the contracts with it. They couldn't take your ACCU's or have any claim on your land ect.- they would just be buying our part of it. * No matter what happens on our end your percentage of the ACCU's are yours. Here is the link for your solicitor to some of the commonly asked questions: https://help.agriprove.io/the-agriprove-contract Let us know and we can lock in a time with you and the solicitor to go through it all. Talk soon. they are using AG360 and are doing it often they have done Prograze, 3 day RCS clinic and the RCS Grazing for Profit Course. They have been applying pasture seed via air- mixed grass species with sub and arrow leaf clovers for legumes. (It is too steep to sow with a tractor). they have agronomist soil test done and they said the thing they needed was Sulfur. they have been applying elemental sulfur with the pasture seed- working through applying to whole place and are almost done. The intention is to get soil test done after the sulfur is done and find out what more they need. They used to use Superphosphate and are now only going to use natural products like the sulfur due to wanting to promote soil microbes. They are aiming for 50ha paddocks for now- will be fencing a big paddock in half to change grazing pressure and allow longer rest on other paddocks. Currently aim for 2 weeks per paddock, but make the decision based on the grass and season, always trying to leave 2-3 inches in the paddock and to maintain groundcover. 2 weeks across the current 6 paddocks is 12 weeks rest. Will plan to feed in a smaller area to protect grass if a drought happened to help maintain carbon too. Said he was never planning to go back to synthetic fertiliser is using legumes for nitrogen- planting the clovers and getting them established in the less fertile areas first, then planting the grass after as the nitrogen helps and have seen the grasses perform better when done this way rather than together.

engagements.subject: AgriProve - Process changes impacting projects registered after 8th November
engagements.body: Hi Tim and Courtney, I hope this message finds you well. I wanted to reach out to keep you informed of an important update that may impact your carbon project registration with AgriProve. The Clean Energy Regulator (CER) is updating some of their processes, and as a result, if we do not receive your sign agreement (Key Commercial Terms) by the 8th November we will need to revise your documentation to ensure we align with their requirements. This will mean additional paperwork for you, and we understand how valuable your time is. To avoid any unnecessary delays, we’re aiming to have all current agreements signed and finalised before 8th November. Please note that signing now does not lock you in to baselining immediately, and we will work with you to schedule sampling at a time that suits you. Invoicing for baselining only occurs after sampling has been completed and results are supplied to you. Our priority is making this as seamless as possible for you and ensuring that your project moves forward without extra hassle. We’re here to support you through this process and ensure that everything is handled smoothly and with your best interests in mind. Called to check in on KCT: It was still with solicitor and the solicitor had concerns. Tim was leaning towards parking it because it seemed all a bit worrying. --> His concerns were around: what if the company goes broke before 25 years, or gets sold to someone eg. a chinese company, what happens if there is no increase or goes backwards. 25 year contract seemed very scary. He also watched a landline piece that said a lot of people regretted it. I explained that there is the potential to stop at 5 years ( would check details for him), that there was dodgy things happening early, explained why we are reputable, what i have seen ( as i know Tim personally). The 5 year out seemed like a good thing that he didnt know about and eased him a bit. Now interested in getting the ball moving again- starting with us talking to his solicitor. I am going to send him the FAQ's and organise that meeting to happen.

engagements.subject: AgriProve Follow up & Solicitor Details
engagements.body: Good Afternoon Tim, Great to chat to you today! Its a very small world. I checked up on a few of the things we spoke about and the answers are below: * As mentioned, there is a few ways out of the contract with that 5 year mark being a major one. Happy to meet your solicitor and go through that. * If AgriProve did go broke - you could transfer your project to another proponent. You would be able to take your sample results elsewhere and continue the project with someone else. This is because the main contract to get ACCUS is with the government, we are the people in the middle helping, but if we voided our end by going broke and not being able to continue you could go elsewhere. * Us being sold to a Chinese company - we cant predict that, but no matter what if someone bought us they would have to honor the project commitment to you as they would be buying the contracts with it. They couldn't take your ACCU's or have any claim on your land ect.- they would just be buying our part of it. * No matter what happens on our end your percentage of the ACCU's are yours. Here is the link for your solicitor to some of the commonly asked questions: https://help.agriprove.io/the-agriprove-contract Let us know and we can lock in a time with you and the solicitor to go through it all. Talk soon. engagements.subject: Carbon Project Questions
engagements.body: Good Morning Tim & Courtney, As a part of our review of your project application we have identified a couple of gaps that we need to confirm prior to finalizing the documents that we will be able to send to your lawyer. We have put together as much as we can from past documents and conversations and just need a couple more details for us to put together a strong application. Could you please answer the below questions: 1. Are you using any tools currently e.g. ag360, Agriwebb, Maia grazing, pasture budgets or others? 2. Do you have any intention of starting to use tools in the future ? 3. Have you attended any courses around grazing in addition to Prograze eg. RCS? 4. What are you planning to change about your grazing going forwards? E.g. Currently you have X paddocks and are going to fence smaller, we are looking to use higher densities, shorter rests, pasture budgeting ect. 5. What species have you been planting ? 6. What soil treatments have you been doing? E.g. The nutrients you mentioned. 7. What planting, fencing and soil treatments do you have planned for the future? ( going forwards for the 25 year project) 8. Do you have any targets or triggers for managing grazing? E.g. We don't try to graze below X height or kg DM, we target X days grazing and Y rest, X cattle per hectare. 9. Do you have targets of what you would like to change in grazing going forwards? E.g. We would like to add alot more fencing to rotational graze, give paddocks more rest ect. 10. What is your plan going forwards to manage for carbon ? E.g. they are using AG360 and are doing it often they have done Prograze, 3 day RCS clinic and the RCS Grazing for Profit Course. They have been applying pasture seed via air- mixed grass species with sub and arrow leaf clovers for legumes. (It is too steep to sow with a tractor). they have agronomist soil test done and they said the thing they needed was Sulfur. they have been applying elemental sulfur with the pasture seed- working through applying to whole place and are almost done. The intention is to get soil test done after the sulfur is done and find out what more they need. They used to use Superphosphate and are now only going to use natural products like the sulfur due to wanting to promote soil microbes. They are aiming for 50ha paddocks for now- will be fencing a big paddock in half to change grazing pressure and allow longer rest on other paddocks. Currently aim for 2 weeks per paddock, but make the decision based on the grass and season, always trying to leave 2-3 inches in the paddock and to maintain groundcover. 2 weeks across the current 6 paddocks is 12 weeks rest. Will plan to feed in a smaller area to protect grass if a drought happened to help maintain carbon too. Said he was never planning to go back to synthetic fertiliser is using legumes for nitrogen- planting the clovers and getting them established in the less fertile areas first, then planting the grass after as the nitrogen helps and have seen the grasses perform better when done this way rather than together.

engagements.subject: AgriProve Follow up & Solicitor Details
engagements.body: Good Afternoon Tim, Great to chat to you today! Its a very small world. I checked up on a few of the things we spoke about and the answers are below: * As mentioned, there is a few ways out of the contract with that 5 year mark being a major one. Happy to meet your solicitor and go through that. * If AgriProve did go broke - you could transfer your project to another proponent. You would be able to take your sample results elsewhere and continue the project with someone else. This is because the main contract to get ACCUS is with the government, we are the people in the middle helping, but if we voided our end by going broke and not being able to continue you could go elsewhere. * Us being sold to a Chinese company - we cant predict that, but no matter what if someone bought us they would have to honor the project commitment to you as they would be buying the contracts with it. They couldn't take your ACCU's or have any claim on your land ect.- they would just be buying our part of it. * No matter what happens on our end your percentage of the ACCU's are yours. Here is the link for your solicitor to some of the commonly asked questions: https://help.agriprove.io/the-agriprove-contract Let us know and we can lock in a time with you and the solicitor to go through it all. engagements.subject: Carbon Project Questions
engagements.body: Good Morning Tim & Courtney, As a part of our review of your project application we have identified a couple of gaps that we need to confirm prior to finalizing the documents that we will be able to send to your lawyer. We have put together as much as we can from past documents and conversations and just need a couple more details for us to put together a strong application. Could you please answer the below questions: 1. Are you using any tools currently e.g. ag360, Agriwebb, Maia grazing, pasture budgets or others? 2. Do you have any intention of starting to use tools in the future ? 3. Have you attended any courses around grazing in addition to Prograze eg. RCS? 4. What are you planning to change about your grazing going forwards? E.g. Currently you have X paddocks and are going to fence smaller, we are looking to use higher densities, shorter rests, pasture budgeting ect. 5. What species have you been planting ? 6. What soil treatments have you been doing? E.g. The nutrients you mentioned. 7. What planting, fencing and soil treatments do you have planned for the future? ( going forwards for the 25 year project) 8. Do you have any targets or triggers for managing grazing? E.g. We don't try to graze below X height or kg DM, we target X days grazing and Y rest, X cattle per hectare. 9. Do you have targets of what you would like to change in grazing going forwards? E.g. We would like to add alot more fencing to rotational graze, give paddocks more rest ect. 10. What is your plan going forwards to manage for carbon ? E.g. Destock if needed, feed to reduce pressure on pasture, maintain groundcover, adjust stocking rate. Once we have these details we can finish this and get the contract to your lawyer right away. If you have any questions, feel free to give me a call, Kind regards, Claudia Claudia Bryant | Customer Success Specialist [AgriProve] Phone: 1300467465 Mobile: +61483969401 Email: claudia@agriprove.io Address: Level 1, 601 Dean Street Albury NSW 2640 [Lynch CP option 1 (1).png] www.agriprove.io [cid:046a7beb-bc6b-40b3-942a-dbf59a710484] [cid:3f3b413e-c0c8-40f4-8989-d6aad51b6940] [cid:ccc97cf1-e15c-4e16-9e05-8a966cea6893] [cid:186e7fe7-e65d-44a6-bf9f-18c8cfbce4a4] Here at AgriProve we care for your privacy. they are using AG360 and are doing it often they have done Prograze, 3 day RCS clinic and the RCS Grazing for Profit Course. They have been applying pasture seed via air- mixed grass species with sub and arrow leaf clovers for legumes. (It is too steep to sow with a tractor). they have agronomist soil test done and they said the thing they needed was Sulfur. they have been applying elemental sulfur with the pasture seed- working through applying to whole place and are almost done. The intention is to get soil test done after the sulfur is done and find out what more they need. They used to use Superphosphate and are now only going to use natural products like the sulfur due to wanting to promote soil microbes. They are aiming for 50ha paddocks for now- will be fencing a big paddock in half to change grazing pressure and allow longer rest on other paddocks. Currently aim for 2 weeks per paddock, but make the decision based on the grass and season, always trying to leave 2-3 inches in the paddock and to maintain groundcover. 2 weeks across the current 6 paddocks is 12 weeks rest. Will plan to feed in a smaller area to protect grass if a drought happened to help maintain carbon too. Said he was never planning to go back to synthetic fertiliser is using legumes for nitrogen- planting the clovers and getting them established in the less fertile areas first, then planting the grass after as the nitrogen helps and have seen the grasses perform better when done this way rather than together.

That is a substantial carbon asset, built on the grazing operation you are already running. Your Vertosol country in particular is well suited to this. Vertosols carry high water holding capacity, high productivity, and high carbon stability, making them one of the best soil types for long-term carbon accumulation under the ERF. Combined with your Chromosol country and 640mm of annual rainfall, the conditions at Castle Hill are genuinely well positioned for a project of this scale. The HORIZON Snapshot attached covers your HORIZON zone map, soil indicators, and two pricing options. engagements.subject: Re: AgriProve Project Information
engagements.body: Thanks again George, Looking forward to confirming our 45 minute Land Management Strategy Call with you on Monday the 25th of May at 2pm. In the meantime to proceed to next steps, there are three things that will help us hit the ground running: Eligible Activities A soil carbon project is built around the land management practices you implement on your property — you'll need to adopt at least two, as long as it's genuinely new or materially different from what you've been doing over the past five years. Click link here to review your choices of Eligible Activities: https://help.agriprove.io/what-is-a-soil-carbon-project Paddock maps for each property — digital files are ideal, but hand-drawn maps showing clear boundary lines work just as well. These let us accurately configure your project areas before the call. Five-year farm management history: https://ap1.hubs.ly/y0HwWH0 — this is one of the most important pieces of the puzzle. To accurately model your soil carbon baseline and project what your land can sequester, we need a clear picture of how your properties have been managed over the past five years. Think stocking rates, pasture management, any significant land use changes — the more detail the better. Don't worry if it's not perfectly documented; we'll work through it together on the call. engagements.body: Hi Neil, I hope you are well and looking forward to the call with you at 1pm. I just wanted to make sure you had a few of the items on hand that I said I would send through on our last call. Firstly, see below Adam Gunthrope article: Beef Central - Adam Gunthrope article: https://www.beefcentral.com/carbon/central-qld-brahman-breeders-soil-carbon-credit-sale-shows-diversified-income-potential/ Secondly, I had a look into your question regarding lucerne and... Yes, lucerne can contribute to increased soil carbon levels. Its deep roots, ability to fix nitrogen, and the creation of soil structure through its growth all play a role in boosting soil health and carbon sequestration. Here's how lucerne helps: Deep Root System: Lucerne's deep roots penetrate the soil, improving drainage and increasing the amount of organic matter deposited at depth. Nitrogen Fixation: Lucerne is a legume that can fix atmospheric nitrogen, enriching the soil and reducing the need for synthetic fertilizers. Soil Structure: Lucerne's roots help to break up soil compaction, improving soil structure and aeration, which further enhances carbon storage. Carbon Sequestration: Lucerne's growth and root decomposition contribute to the build-up of soil organic matter, which is a key component of soil carbon. And below is a link to the definitions around "new' or 'material differences in eligible practices : AgriProve eligible practices: https://help.agriprove.io/is-my-farm-eligible-for-a-soil-carbon-project I have the team looking into your other questions which I hope to have address for you this week and I'm sure there will be more questions after our call. engagements.body: Hi Jackie and Morgan, Thank you very much for your patience while I came back to you with the additional information we require after our call last week. To assist with the project scoping process, I would like into introduce Ben Payne, Account Manager at AgriProve, who will be helping to bring all the information together for your final project proposal. At this stage could you please: Check that all property boundaries have been included in the below maps. If land titles have been missed, please identify them. Provided the AgriWebb paddock map KML. files for the properties. Confirm the total hectares that single super and lime were applied to for each year from 2020-2025. Confirm that the average stocking rate was 575 Breeders, 575 Calves, 10 Bulls for 2020-2025? Could you please provide either AgriWebb stock data or stock numbers based on the sale data for 2020-2025? (Why? Although the average numbers will be great for project registration. It will be important to have more exact numbers for later emissions accounting purposes.) Can you please provide the hectares of improve pasture each year from 2020-2025 and if applicable the number of hectares tillage each year and number of passes (direct drilling doesn't count as tillage but ploughing or scarifying for a oat pasture might be examples). If you have any questions, please feel free to ring as this can often save a lot of time and hassle for you. Once we have this information we look forward to commencing the mapping process. engagements.body: Hi Jacklyn, I just wanted to let you know that the National Carbon Farming Conference & Expo is on in Albury from 3rd to 6th November.
